text.p: Honeywell Inc. reported record earnings Tuesday for the first quarter due to strong orders for its control systems for home and aerospace uses.
First quarter profits rose 16 percent to $75.6 million from $65.1 million in the same period last year. Earnings per share went up to 60 cents from 51 cents last year, an increase of 18 percent.
Orders were strong, led by the home and building and space and aviation control businesses, said Chairman Michael Bonsignore.
Profits in space and aviation grew to $51.9 million from $39.1 million a year ago, due to strong growth in commerical avionics, the company said. Orders were up 19 percent.

Home and building controls profit was up 8 percent, to $57.9 million from $53.8 million last year. Honeywell said this was due to several key contracts plus sales of its consumer products at Sears and the production of Sears-brand products.

Industrial controls showed a decrease in profits to $45 million from $50 million in the same period last year. Honeywell said it was due to expenses after the aquisition of automation solution company Measurex Corp. and productivity initiatives.
